blocks.text: WRN:000–022 DETAILED REVIEW AND DELEGATED APPROVAL — CANONICAL

The Warning entity block was reconsidered from first principles under the standing delegated authority. The review compared five genuinely different architectures per root, scored 45 candidates across 360 criterion values, routed 92 English concepts without forced atomization, passed all 18 canonical packet checks, passed all 18 Warning entity-layer soundness checks, and passed the complete 29-check authority regression. All deterministic generated forms remained unchanged.

Approved architecture: WRN:0xx names adverse-condition entities. The inward triplet names an intrinsic fault within one reference entity; the outward triplet names a distinct external hazard relative to one reference target; and the systemic triplet names one correlated distributed fault across multiple participants. The third trit changes only persistent identity, present harmful manifestation, or dormant/nonmanifest status.
WRN:000 — persistent internal fault — An intrinsic adverse condition that remains identified within one reference entity independently of whether it is presently producing harmful deviation.
WRN:001 — manifest internal fault — An intrinsic adverse condition within one reference entity that is presently producing harmful deviation from that entity's accepted state.
WRN:002 — latent internal fault — An intrinsic adverse condition within one reference entity that is present without presently producing harmful deviation.
WRN:010 — persistent external hazard — A distinct external condition that remains identified as capable of adversely affecting one reference target independently of current contact or effect.
WRN:011 — manifest external hazard — A distinct external condition that is presently expressing the harmful potential by which it can adversely affect one reference target.
WRN:012 — dormant external hazard — A distinct external condition capable of adversely affecting one reference target that is present without presently expressing that harmful potential.

WRN:020 — persistent distributed fault — One correlated adverse condition that remains identified across multiple participant entities within a shared system independently of its present manifestation pattern.
WRN:021 — manifest distributed fault — One correlated adverse condition that is presently producing harmful deviation across multiple participant entities within a shared system.
WRN:022 — latent distributed fault — One correlated adverse condition present across multiple participant entities within a shared system without presently producing harmful deviation.

Design boundary: these roots do not silently encode bearers, physical mechanisms, evidence, observer belief, alarms or warning messages, formal invalidity, severity, probability, cause, attack or propagation processes, vulnerability or exposure relations, response, containment, or repair. A persistent root may co-occur with its manifest or dormant sibling; manifest and dormant are mutually exclusive for the same condition at one reference time. Lexical third-trit status remains distinct from runtime [0], [1], or [2]/num.
